newsitem.title: EGYPT: Followers of Egyptian sheikh warn America.
newsitem.headline: Followers of Egyptian sheikh warn America.

text.p: Followers of Egyptian Islamist leader Sheikh Omar Abdel-Rahman, who is ailing in prison in Missouri, have sent him a message of reassurance that the United States will not get away with the way it has treated him.

"We will not let America do what it likes. Our tryst with the Americans is close at hand, God willing," the Jihad Movement-Vanguards of Conquest said in a message to the sheikh, copied to an international news agency on Thursday.
The organisation is one of several dedicated to overthrowing Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak by violence and turning Egypt into a strict Islamic state.

Lawyers for the sheikh, jailed on charges of conspiracy to blow up the United Nations and other New York City landmarks, say his health is deteriorating because of his solitary confinement in Springfield federal prison.

An Islamist organisation in Europe has called for half-hour sit-ins in European mosques after Friday prayers next week in solidarity with the blind preacher, the international Arabic-language newspaper al-Hayat said on Thursday.
The sheikh, who migrated to the United States in the 1980s, has grown into a symbol of Sunni Moslem fundamentalist opposition to Western influence in the Arab world.

The Jihad Movement told the sheikh he deserved better than to be jailed in America. "The likes of you should be raised high, cherished and protected from the guile of the criminal enemies of Islam, not put in prisons and cells," it said.
"But patience, sheikh, for you have taught us that vanity takes its turn for but one hour, while the truth lasts until the Hour of Judgment," it added.
It was not clear if or how the message, dated Wednesday, would reach the sheikh in his cell.
